questions.q: A loan model trained without any group column still approves 58% of group A but only 37% of group B. What is the most likely explanation?
options: Fairlearn introduced the gap
Other features correlate with group, so the model reconstructs the pattern anyway
The model must be secretly reading the group column
Selection rate is not a meaningful metric
questions.explain: Removing a sensitive column does not remove its influence when other features (income, region) correlate with it. This is why you measure outcomes by group.

questions.q: Which is NOT one of the three stages of model debugging described in the lesson?
options: Identify
Diagnose
Mitigate
Advertise
questions.explain: Microsoft's framing is identify (errors and fairness issues), diagnose (why they happen), and mitigate (targeted fixes).

questions.q: Which open-source project provides the fairness assessment capability in the Responsible AI dashboard?
options: DiCE
EconML
Fairlearn
InterpretML
questions.explain: Fairlearn powers fairness. DiCE does counterfactuals, EconML causal inference and InterpretML explanations.

questions.q: A counterfactual tool such as DiCE is best described as doing what?
options: Searching for the smallest feature change that flips a model's prediction
Retraining the model on more data
Measuring how much production data has drifted
Encrypting the training dataset
questions.explain: Counterfactuals show the closest data point with a different outcome, e.g. the change an applicant could make to be approved.

questions.q: What does the fairness tooling tell you about the 21-point gap in selection rate between two groups?
options: That the model is definitely illegal
That the gap is always acceptable if accuracy is high
That the gap will disappear if you retrain
It measures the gap; whether it is justified is a human and policy decision
questions.explain: Tools quantify disparities. Deciding which fairness definition to enforce and whether a gap is justified requires human judgment, domain knowledge and often legal input.
